papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.why: The most-cited paper of the century: skip connections made very deep networks trainable, and they're in every modern architecture.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.why: Introduced the transformer, the architecture behind essentially every modern language model.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.why: Low-rank fine-tuning.

papers.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
papers.why: The first direct detection of gravitational waves, a century after Einstein predicted them.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.why: Showed loss falls as a smooth power law in model size, data and compute: the intellectual basis for the scaling era.

papers.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
papers.why: The default optimizer of deep learning, and one of the most-cited papers ever.

papers.title: The sphere packing problem in dimension 8
papers.why: A short, beautiful proof using modular forms that won a Fields Medal.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
papers.why: Made pre-train-then-fine-tune the standard recipe for language understanding.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.why: The paper that made diffusion models work, the basis of modern image and video generation.

papers.title: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
papers.why: Solved a 50-year grand challenge in biology and won a Nobel Prize.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
papers.why: The origin of RLHF, the technique that turned language models into assistants.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
papers.why: InstructGPT: how RLHF was scaled up into what became ChatGPT.

papers.title: Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture
papers.why: A two-page proof that settled a 30-year-old open problem in computer science.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.why: Brought transformers to vision and started the convergence of architectures across fields.

papers.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
papers.why: Chinchilla: corrected the scaling laws and changed how every lab splits compute between parameters and data.

papers.title: Quantum supremacy using a programmable superconducting processor
papers.why: Google's first demonstration of a quantum computer beating classical simulation on a task.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.why: Showed that letting models reason step by step unlocks new abilities, the seed of today's reasoning models.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.why: CLIP: joined images and language in one space, the backbone of text-to-image systems.

papers.title: Small gaps between primes
papers.why: A landmark in number theory: bounded gaps between primes with a surprisingly simple method.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.why: The workhorse reinforcement-learning algorithm, used in RLHF for years.

papers.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
papers.why: The idea behind most frontier models today: only part of the network runs for each token.

papers.title: First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole
papers.why: The first image of a black hole, from a planet-sized telescope.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.why: Showed that thinking about memory, not just maths, made attention several times faster.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.why: Training a model to follow written principles using AI feedback instead of only human labels.

papers.title: Strong bounds for 3-progressions
papers.why: A huge jump on a classic problem in additive combinatorics, by two computer scientists.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.why: Replaced the RL step of RLHF with a simple loss, now used across the field.
